g5ela-18-1-listen-words: Two word parts run through this whole book. One is about remembering. One is about writing. Isaac is doing both. Try to find them before the page tells you. When you get to the river game, say each word slowly and listen for where your voice stops.
g5ela-18-2-listen-words: Today you match each word to its root, and you read this week's words in sentences from the book. In the river game, say each word slowly and listen for where your voice stops.
g5ela-18-3-listen-words: Today you build appositives yourself and use your roots to work out words you have never seen. The river game has root stones now. Tap only the letters of the root.
g5ela-18-4-listen-words: Last day with these roots. Build the words from their pieces, then use this week's words in your own sentences. Finish your river crossing too.
g5ela-19-1-listen-words: Two roots this week. One means life. One means breath. Long ago, people thought those were almost the same thing. Look for them in words you already know. Then three endings that turn a word into a describing word. In the footprint game, say each word out loud before you pick an ending.
g5ela-19-2-listen-words: You met the life root and the breath root. Now decide which one is hiding in each word. Some words carry both ideas. Then sort the describing words by their endings. Find the smaller word inside first. Then the footprint game has six new words to build.
g5ela-19-3-listen-words: Today you put the roots to work. In Spelling, the words are new. Build each describing word in your head before you place it. If the base ends in a silent e, check whether it stays or goes. The footprint game works the same way.
g5ela-19-4-listen-words: Last day with life and breath. Today you explain why one idea needed two roots. In Spelling, the words change in different ways when an ending is added. Sometimes a silent e drops. Sometimes the base changes more. Sometimes nothing changes. Look closely at the base each time.
g5ela-20-1-listen-words: Two new roots this week, and both are about feeling. One leans toward emotion. One leans toward the senses. Then listen to long words. When a word grows, its strongest beat can move. In the council fire game, say each word out loud and tap the beat you say the strongest.
g5ela-20-2-listen-words: Today you decide which feeling root is in each word: the one for emotion, or the one for the senses. Then sort words by where the stress falls. Say each word twice, leaning on a different beat each time. Only one way sounds right.
g5ela-20-3-listen-words: Put the feeling roots to work today. Then the spelling words: when a vowel is too quiet to hear, say a related word where that beat is strong. The vowel comes back. The council fire game uses the same trick.
g5ela-20-4-listen-words: Last day with the feeling roots. Explain the difference between feeling with someone and feeling from inside their experience. In spelling, the vowel you cannot hear hides in the quiet beat. Find a relative that makes it loud.
g5ela-21-1-listen-words: Two roots this week, and both are about sight. One means see. One means look. Then words that sound the same but are spelled differently. A spell checker will not catch them. In the spyglass game, find the root first, then the meaning.
g5ela-21-2-listen-words: Today you decide which root each word carries: see, or look. Then sort the sound alike words by the job they do. Does the word show who owns something, name a thing, or squeeze two words together? Then five new words in the spyglass.
g5ela-21-3-listen-words: Put the sight roots to work today. Then the sound alike words again, sorted a new way: is the word a thing, an action, or two words squeezed? Say it in a sentence to check. Then five new words in the spyglass.
g5ela-21-4-listen-words: Last day with the sight roots. Explain the difference between looking and seeing. Then the academic pairs that trip up even grown writers: affect and effect, principal and principle. Then the last five words in the spyglass.
